instructions: Set racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven and heat it to 200°F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper.
Wash the 3 apples and core them with an apple corer, or leave the cores in if you don't mind a few seeds.
Slice the apples across into rounds about 1/8 inch thick, with a mandoline if you have one.
Lay the slices on the baking sheets in a single layer and sprinkle the 3/4 tsp cinnamon over them.
Swap the pans between the upper and lower racks. Bake for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until a slice you take out and leave on the counter for 2 to 3 minutes is crisp.
Turn off the oven and leave the chips inside for 1 hour as it cools, so they crisp up more. If they already look dark, take them out and cool them on the counter instead.
Serve them at room temperature. They keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week.
method_notes: Both slice apples into thin rounds, dust them with cinnamon and dry them slowly in a low oven for about 2 hours, then let them crisp as the oven cools. Well Plated (the lead) uses 3 large sweet apples and 3/4 tsp cinnamon at 200°F, swaps the pans after an hour, tests one chip on the counter and keeps them up to a week. Running on Real Food bakes at 220°F and flips the slices after an hour. This follows the lead, which makes about 3 cups.
